P16-001.challenge_claim: The row asserts that its governing frame recurs verbatim at byte tier between its two cited verses, and the bytes refuse it — the two forms differ in pointing, not merely accents, and reach only consonantal tier against each other.
P16-001.grounds: Re-derived; OL is exactly right, including its diagnosis of the cause. It fails even the accent-stripped tier because the divergence is in the POINTING, not the accents: the opening letter carries a dagesh at MT 56:1 and none at MT 56:4, so accent-stripping cannot equalise the two. 'Recurs verbatim at byte tier' is therefore FALSE as written, and it is the row's stated ground for holding the whole span as one admission unit. A second respect in which the two are not one object: the MT 56:4 instance is not verse-initial — the verse opens כִּי, subordinating the frame, where MT 56:1 stands verse-initial. Added digit: the MT 56:1 pointed run stands at byte tier in exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, MT 43:16, 56:1, 66:1). Second item UPHELD, scoped: נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה occupies the FIRST three tokens of MT 56:8 — verse-initial — and heads the gathering clause it is said to seal, and the WEB rendering likewise places the formula ahead of the quoted speech at web:Isa.56.8. The formula CLASS is postpositive book-wide, so the class label is not a fabrication; this INSTANCE is not postpositive, so 'closes on ... which seals' is a position claim the bytes refuse. Third item UPHELD: the byte-identical closing run shared by MT 55:13 and MT 56:5 straddles this row's front seam undisclosed here too (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses; skeleton 3 verses) — the same seam-pair edit ordered on the row ending at web:Isa.55.13. Fourth, OL's unused-unity point is byte-exact and is the evidence the row actually needs: שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ is BYTE-IDENTICAL at MT 56:2 and MT 56:6 (sweep: 2 verses, the only two in the book) and וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי is byte-identical at MT 56:4 and MT 56:6 (sweep: 2 verses) — a byte refrain pair bracketing the third-person turn the row argues across. Credit verified: frame ownership is right (both cited sites sit on the divine side, the four royal-messenger sites stay in the narrative zone); the MT 56:8 divine-name object is correctly named as the stacked title-plus-tetragrammaton form rather than the bare title; and mark handling is exact — SAMEKH at MT 56:2, 56:3 and 56:5 plus the front-seam seg at MT 55:13, petuchah never conflated, the MT 56:4 paseq disclosed count-only with no intra-verse position, and 0 ketiv/qere notes across MT 56:1-56:8. The rival the row does disclose lies wholly inside the feminine stretch and is, as OL says, the weaker of the two candidates. NEW FINDING: the other primary's SUPPORT for this row is byte-refuted on this exact point — it credits a second-person indictment running unbroken and a sustained address, which the plural-to-feminine-singular turn contradicts. Second item UPHELD with its tiers exact but its weight scoped: וְנִשָּׂ֔א at oshb:Isa.57.7 and וְנִשָּׂ֗א at oshb:Isa.57.15 are NOT byte-identical (the MT 57:7 form stands at byte tier in exactly 1 verse book-wide) and are identical at ACCENT-STRIPPED tier, where the form stands in 6 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses, MT 2:2, 6:1, 39:6, 52:13, 57:7, 57:15) — OL's list re-derived exactly — and MT 57:7 / MT 57:15 are its only two sites inside one chapter, straddling this row's closing seam undisclosed. The omission of כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י לֵ֚ךְ (oshb:Isa.21.6, byte tier, the intervening-dative member) is likewise not a defect: the row writes 'also carried at', claims no exhaustive set, and so owes no digit. LF's item is UPHELD at low: device_notes calls the distant comparison 'cross-part texture', naming the writer's own batch structure rather than the two verses' relationship in Isaiah's text — barred in every field. The 2-verse digit belongs to the UNPREFIXED core: that object stands in exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT 59:8 and MT 59:15), its partner being אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט at oshb:Isa.59.15. A reproduced digit carrying the wrong count-object is itself the defect class the campaign names; the underlying finding — a two-site pairing on this row's own closing verse whose partner sits past the seam — survives on the corrected object. OL's inclusio item is UPHELD and verified: the salvation root inside the row's own opening splice, מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ, returns at וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע (oshb:Isa.59.16) and וְכ֥וֹבַע יְשׁוּעָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.59.17), all byte tier — the salvation family, correctly kept apart from the prophet's name, which shares consonants but not this order.
